summary: Walkthrough of Opal Finance vendor risk questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ) with focus on encryption/KMS, audit logs, RBAC/SSO, SOC 2 evidence. Redwood team outlined where evidence lives, acceptable redaction patterns, and options for Private/VPC deployment. Agreed to deliver KMS artifacts and SOC 2 link; Opal to confirm residency requirements and specific vendor-form fields. Follow-up technical session for VPC by end of July.
topics: Encryption key management: KMS vs HSM, customer keys
Audit logs retention and access controls
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We can do intros quick — I'm Maya, AE on the account. Ethan and Priya from Redwood will walk through the SIG/CAIQ package and answer any evidence questions.
[00:00:18] Lena: Thanks, Maya. I'm Lena, CISO at Opal. We've got a vendor security form with about 260 questions, and the procurement team wants the SIG mapped answers plus supporting evidence where possible.
[00:00:34] Ethan: Great, we prepared a mapping sheet that aligns SIG controls to the Opal form, and we've flagged items that need artifacts. We'll share the sheet after the call.
[00:00:42] Tomás: Quick Q before we start — what's your acceptable redaction policy for SOC items? Legal likes to see high-level control descriptions but redacted customer data is fine.
[00:00:55] Priya: We usually provide SOC 2 Type II report redacted for customer-specific data; the redaction guidelines are in the doc we shared. We can also provide system-level diagrams and control narratives.
[00:01:08] Ravi: On the KMS front — does Redwood support customer-managed keys (CMK) or only platform-managed KMS? We need to know for encryption-in-use and long-term retention.
[00:01:22] Ethan: Short answer: both, depending on deployment. On Hosted we offer platform-managed KMS with envelope encryption; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations and HSM-backed options. There are operational differences.
[00:01:38] [00:01:40] Lena: Can you walk us through the evidence we would get for KMS? We need key rotation policies, access logs, and evidence of HSM if used.
[00:01:50] Priya: Sure — evidence package typically includes key lifecycle policy doc, sample audit logs showing key access events, and HSM attestation or vendor cert if HSM is in use. We can also provide architecture diagrams showing separation of duties.
[00:02:10] Ethan: I'll flag that in the SIG sheet as "requires artifact" and attach a KMS diagram. Note: for hosted customers, keys may be customer-specific logical keys but still managed by Redwood's KMS; for private deploy we can accept customer's KMS endpoint.
[00:02:30] Tomás: About audit logs — what's the retention, and can we get S3-delivered log copies for our archival?
[00:02:40] Priya: Default is 90 days in the console for hosted telemetry; we have add-ons for longer retention and object store export. For Dedicated/Private you can configure export to your S3 bucket in your VPC.
[00:02:55] Ravi: Do the logs contain PII? We have to know for GDPR and retention.
[00:03:02] Ethan: Logs are redacted for PII in the standard pipeline; we can provide sanitized logs for evidence. If you want raw logs in your own S3 we can support that in private deployments but that requires a dataflow agreement.
[00:03:18] [00:03:20] Lena: Let's go through a few SIG control families. Section A: Access Control. How does RBAC look in Redwood?
[00:03:31] Ethan: RBAC is role-based with built-in roles (Admin, Operator, Observer) and you can create custom roles with allowed API scopes. We support SCIM for provisioning and SAML 2.0 for SSO.
[00:03:45] Maya: To add, session policies and token expiry are configurable per-tenant in Dedicated. We can share our RBAC matrix.
[00:03:55] Tomás: Do you log admin activity for auditing?
[00:03:58] Priya: Yes — admin actions are logged with timestamp, actor, IP, and resource, and we retain those logs per your selected retention plan. We can provide examples of the audit log schema.
[00:04:10] [00:04:12] Ravi: For SCIM provisioning, do you support user-deprovisioning hooks? We need automated removal within 15 minutes of AD account disablement.
[00:04:22] Ethan: We support SCIM delta provisioning and event-driven deprovisioning; typical sync interval is configurable, and in Dedicated we can tune it to meet <15 min SLAs. We'll note that as a configuration option.
[00:04:36] Lena: Onto network controls — VPC peering and private endpoints. If we go private, can we ensure no egress to the public internet?
[00:04:47] Priya: Private deployments can be fully network-isolated, with private endpoints and optional air-gapped setups. For hosted, we have region-level isolation but there are egress paths through managed NAT. We'll outline the options.
[00:05:00] Maya: Also worth noting capacity: Dedicated pools are single-tenant for compute but control plane may remain in Redwood-managed control unless you choose our Private package.
[00:05:10] [00:05:12] Tomás: On SOC 2 — is the control scope covering ops and infra only, or also customer data handling?
[00:05:20] Priya: Our SOC 2 scope covers the Redwood hosted service and operational controls; we provide a mapping document that indicates which controls apply to Dedicated/Private. We'll put that in the evidence packet.
[00:05:33] [00:05:35] Ravi: A question about key compromise: what is your incident response playbook, and do you have forensic logs for key usage?
[00:05:44] Ethan: We have an IR runbook with escalation paths, and for key compromise we can revoke and rotate keys, with replayable audit trails. Forensics depend on deployment — Private gives you fuller access to raw telemetry. We'll provide redacted runbook excerpts.
[00:06:02] [00:06:05] Lena: I'm scanning your SIG answers — a couple of places you marked "see backup" — can you be more specific on what those backups look like?
[00:06:16] Priya: "Backup" in our sheet generally refers to encrypted object backups with immutable retention options. We'll attach a sample manifest and S3 lifecycle policy.
[00:06:29] [00:06:30] Ravi: About encryption in transit — TLS cipher suites and mutual TLS?
[00:06:35] Ethan: We enforce TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; mutual TLS is available for inter-service or for private endpoints if you require mTLS.
[00:06:45] [00:06:47] Tomás: Evidence delivery — we need to know what you'll redact. Will you remove client names from logs or replace them?
[00:06:55] Priya: We favor redaction with consistent placeholders, and we provide a redaction index so you can validate there was no PII leakage. SOC report redactions are standard; for logs we can sanitize or provide copies to your S3 in private deployments.
[00:07:10] [00:07:12] Lena: Can you show an example of an audit log event?
[00:07:16] Ethan: Sure — paste example (sanitized): {"ts":"2025-06-30T12:23:11Z","actor":"admin:1234","action":"key.rotate","resource":"kms/key/abcd","ip":"52.10.11.34"} — we'll include schema doc.
[00:07:34] [00:07:36] Tomás: Regarding legal — do you accept standard indemnity and data processing terms?
[00:07:43] Maya: We have a standard DPA and security addendum; for enterprise deals we can negotiate limited indemnities. Our legal team can take your redlines. We'll route to contracts.
[00:07:56] [00:07:58] Ravi: On the SIG matrix you left some controls as "see alternative control". For control A.9.4 (user authentication), what's the alternative?
[00:08:08] Priya: The alternative is compensating control: we enforce strict session timeouts, MFA enforcement, and SCIM provisioning with approval flows. We'll put the justification in the comment column.
[00:08:22] [00:08:25] Lena: For data residency: we need EU-only storage for some datasets. Can you pin model artifacts and embeddings to EU regions only?
[00:08:34] Ethan: Yes — in Dedicated and Private you can pin storage and compute to a region. For hosted customers we have EU regions and can restrict tenant placement, but some features (like cross-region fallback) may use other regions unless you select residency-only SKU.
[00:08:52] Maya: We also have a data residency add-on that ensures no backups leave region. We'll include the SLA and SKU options in the packet.
[00:09:05] [00:09:07] Tomás: Let's talk about evidence format: do you deliver a single zip with PDFs and logs, or a link-based repo? Procurement prefers one-time zip with manifest.
[00:09:18] Priya: We typically create a secured shared folder with manifest and downloadable zips for each control family. For Opal, if you prefer the zip manifest we can do that.
[00:09:28] [00:09:30] Ravi: One last technical: model weights and KV cache — are model weights accessible to customers in private deployment? We have IP concerns.
[00:09:40] Ethan: For Private on-prem, you can have full control over model artifacts; for Dedicated we host weights but we can sign an addendum for usage. KV cache is ephemeral and stored in memory or short-term disk depending on config; we do not persist user prompts unless configured for evals with opt-in.
[00:09:58] [00:10:00] Lena: Good. Let's flag high-risk items: 1) KMS evidence 2) RBAC provisioning SLA 3) Data residency confirmation 4) Audit log raw access — those are blockers for security approval.
[00:10:12] Maya: Understood — we will prioritize. Ethan will collect KMS artifacts; Priya will add SOC and control narratives; we'll deliver by Friday.
[00:10:22] [00:10:25] Tomás: Can you include any third-party pen test reports? Procurement asks for recent tests within last 12 months.
[00:10:33] Priya: We have a redacted pentest summary and remediation notes; full report is available under NDA — we can start the NDA if you want.
[00:10:42] Lena: NDA would be fine.
[00:10:45] [00:10:47] Ethan: I'll open the ticket to share NDA and the pentest path.
[00:10:51] [00:10:53] Tomás: How do you handle subprocessor lists? We need a current vendor list and data flow diagram.
[00:11:00] Priya: We'll share our subprocessor roster and a data flow diagram. For any subprocessors that store PHI or sensitive data we call that out.
[00:11:11] [00:11:13] Ravi: A couple of nitty-gritty SIG items — are secrets rotated programmatically? What's the rotation cadence?
[00:11:20] Ethan: Secrets rotation is automated for service-to-service keys; typical cadence is 90 days for service credentials, and customer keys follow your KMS policy. We'll include config examples.
[00:11:33] [00:11:35] Lena: Okay, I want to make sure we have timelines. If we get the evidence by Friday, how long for procurement to review and request follow-ups? Tomás?
[00:11:44] Tomás: Usually 7–10 business days for initial review, more if they need raw artifacts. We'll aim to finish vendor assessment by August if you can meet the evidence deadlines.
[00:11:57] [00:12:00] Maya: Noted. Anything else?
[00:12:04] Tomás: One last thing — do you support searchable immutable audit trails for compliance? We may need e-discovery for legal holds.
[00:12:12] Priya: Yes, we have an audit indexer that can produce immutable search views; for Hosted it's an add-on, for Dedicated it's configurable and for Private you can host the index yourself. We'll include examples of search queries.
[00:12:28] [00:12:30] Ravi: Can we get a sample SLA for incident response times?
[00:12:35] Maya: We'll share our enterprise SLA: 1 hour P1, 4 hours P2 initial response for Dedicated/Private, different for Hosted. We'll attach the SLA doc.
[00:12:48] [00:12:50] Tomás: Great.
[00:12:52] Lena: Okay, wrap up — recap the deliverables?
[00:12:56] Maya: Recap: Redwood to deliver SIG/CAIQ mapping with artifacts, SOC 2 link, KMS/HSM evidence, pentest NDA, data residency SKU options, and schedule a VPC technical walkthrough.
[00:13:12] Priya: We'll also provide RBAC matrix, audit log schema, and a sample sanitized log bundle.
[00:13:20] Ethan: I'll take KMS and technical configuration items.
[00:13:24] Tomás: I'll follow up with procurement timelines and the specific vendor form fields we need answered first.
[00:13:30] [00:13:32] Lena: Thanks everyone. That was helpful.
[00:13:35] Maya: Thanks — we'll send the packet by Friday and book the follow-up.
[00:13:40] [End of recording — transcript truncated to highlights. Full artifacts to be attached in shared folder.]
